real_life_notes: General Shamshad Hassan is the name of a real Pakistani diplomat (Foreign Secretary 1997-2000, during Nawaz Sharif's government and the IC-814 period), but the film's character is depicted as a Pakistani military general — suggesting the film is either using the name as coincidence or conflating the diplomat with a military figure. Most likely a composite of General Hamid Gul (former ISI chief, the ideological godfather of the jihadi-military nexus) and General Pervez Musharraf (COAS 1998-2007, Chief Executive/President).

real_life_composites.hamid_gul: ISI chief 1987-1989. Credited with building the Afghan mujahideen network. Never abandoned his belief in strategic use of jihadists against India. Ideologically closest to the 'military-jihad nexus' the film depicts.
real_life_composites.pervez_musharraf: COAS during Kargil (1999), seized power in coup (October 1999), President until 2008. Officially condemned 26/11 but was simultaneously running ISI operations. His era is the exact timeline of Film 1.
real_life_composites.ashfaq_kayani: COAS 2007-2013 — the 'Bade Sahab' era. Most directly responsible for the 26/11 period.

film_role: Film 1 — Pakistani military authority that provides the institutional cover for Major Iqbal's operations. General Shamshad Hassan is the on-screen military face that interacts with Pakistani political figures (Nawab Shafiq) while Bade Sahab operates in the shadows.
objective: Maintain Pakistani military's strategic depth doctrine; protect ISI's jihadist assets; manage political-military relationship
